title: Reload a long-arm stapler (one hand holds its sprung magazine out, the other lays in staples), then staple two sheets
instruction: Reload the long-arm stapler, then staple the two sheets of paper together: with one hand pull its staple magazine out by the red tab at its back and hold it out; with the other take the strip of staples from the tray and lay it in the open channel; then let the magazine slide back in and let go. Next slide the two sheets on the paper rest in under the stapler's head, up to the paper guide, press the stapler's top arm down to staple them, and pull the stapled sheets back out from under the head onto the paper rest. Finally take both arms back to where they started.
context: Refilling and using a stapler is an everyday office and school chore. On many staplers the magazine is spring-loaded and snaps shut the moment it is let go, so one hand holds it open while the other drops the new strip in; only then does the stapler staple. The job ends with stapled pages, not just a loaded stapler.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A long-arm (booklet) stapler, fixed, lying along the left-right line 30 cm forward, its nose to the left: a grey powder-coated steel base 6 cm wide and 1.5 cm tall running from 19 cm right to 30 cm left of the centre line, widening by its nose (from 17 to 30 cm left) into a flat paper rest that reaches 12 cm forward, with a black steel paper guide (8 mm tall) along its far edge under the head and a chrome anvil 26.5 cm left of the centre line; a black steel magazine housing (4.5 cm wide) over the base from 4 to 29 cm left, 1.4 cm above it (the throat the paper goes into); and a black steel top arm with a red rubber press pad near its nose, hinged on the housing's back end and sprung up 4 degrees (pressed down flat, it pushes back with about 3 N at the pad). (2) Its staple magazine: a steel channel 22 cm long (2 cm wide inside) that runs inside the housing; a red tab (1.2 x 1.6 cm, 3.2 cm tall) stands up at its back end, 3.4 cm left of the centre line. It pulls out to the right up to 20 cm against a spring (4 N fully out) and springs back in when let go. (3) A light wooden tray 6 x 12 cm, 20 cm forward and 9 cm left of the centre line, with a fresh strip of steel staples on it (7 cm long, 1.2 cm wide, 8 mm tall, 30 g) lying along the left-right line. (4) Two sheets of paper (10 x 7 cm, 8 g each), a white printed one on a pale yellow one, lying on the paper rest out from under the head, the white one's middle 21.5 cm forward and 25 cm left of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. 1.0: the stapler loaded (the strip of staples lying in the magazine's channel, its middle within 8 mm of the channel's middle line, along it within 15 degrees, and the magazine slid back within 5 mm of shut), the two sheets stapled together, both sheets pulled back out from under the head (every corner short of the housing) and lying flat on the paper rest, both hands let go (each gripper's fingertip centre, TCP, at least 4 cm from the magazine's tab, the strip, the press pad and the top sheet) and both arms back where they started (each TCP within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: the stapler loaded and the sheets stapled together; 0.25: the stapler loaded; else 0.0. A staple goes in only when the top arm is pressed down at least 3 degrees while the stapler is loaded and both sheets lie flat on the base with the staple point at least 5 mm inside each, so loading must come first. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the magazine, the strip, the top arm and both sheets still.
reset_notes: Pull the magazine out, take the strip out and lay it back on its tray (the magazine springs shut); put two fresh unstapled sheets back on the paper rest.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the stapler is fixed; the magazine is a channel on a sprung slide, the strip of staples one rigid bar, the sheets stiff 3 mm boards. Stapling is a rule: pressing the arm with a loaded stapler over both sheets puts a staple on the top sheet and fixes the two sheets together. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
